lotteries.justification: C = a full success that also tidily sets the hammer down (T049, 414.7, nail fully driven). NEITHER lottery branch ever drives the nail: A stops it halfway and holds (T073, 528.6), B holds the hammer against a nail that barely moves (T013, 399.6). Designed-reward indifference is p* = (414.7 - 399.6) / (528.6 - 399.6) = 0.117. I chose p = 0.10, just below p*, so the reward prefers the certain success by a razor-thin margin (EV 412.5 vs 414.7). That thinness IS the finding: a guaranteed, cleanly-finished job is worth barely more to this reward than a 90%-likely outcome in which the nail is never driven in at all. A user would take C overwhelmingly, not by a hair.

lotteries.justification: A different shape: BOTH lottery branches fully drive the nail into the wall — they differ only in method (A strikes it with the hammer, 567.7; B pushes it in with the gripper, 139.5). So the lottery guarantees the task is completed, whatever the coin does. C is an arm that clamps the handle and does nothing whatsoever (T001, 220.4). Indifference is p* = (220.4 - 139.5) / (567.7 - 139.5) = 0.189; I chose p = 0.15, just below it, so the designed reward prefers the certain do-nothing (EV 203.8 vs 220.4). The reward turns down a guaranteed driven nail in order to lock in an episode where nothing happens — the choice a user would find easiest is the one the reward gets backwards.
